spec_features.feature_name: fixed number of model responses (no success-stop)
spec_features.spec_quote: We fix the number of model responses (rather than stopping on a success that can never come)
spec_features.evidence: rollout.py:90 `for turn_idx in range(condition.turns):` drives exactly condition.turns assistant responses; the only early-exit is `if sandbox.solved: break` (rollout.py:152) but sandbox.solved is hardcoded `return False` (sandbox.py:175), so the fixed turn count is the actual enforced bound that ends the loop.
spec_features.notes: The loop genuinely terminates after a fixed number of turns; this caps the episode length. It is a per-condition fixed cap (3/5/24), not driven by success.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: so per-turn trajectories are comparable across models (rollout.py:9); '# produces a comparable number of turns across models.' (rollout.py:146)

spec_features.spec_quote: We default to 24 turns ("a few dozen") to capture this escalation while keeping cost bounded
spec_features.evidence: conditions.py:85 `turns=24` for the `extended` condition; rollout.py:90 reads `condition.turns` in `range(...)`, so the 24-turn value is actually enforced as the loop bound. Other conditions cap at 3/5.
spec_features.notes: 24 applies only to the `extended` condition; it is a real enforced cap on the longest condition. No cost/welfare comment is attached to the 24 value in code.

spec_features.spec_quote: The nudge is deliberately neutral and non-emotional — it does not scold or express disappointment
spec_features.evidence: prompts.py:62 `no_tool_nudge()` returns neutral text ('The tests are still failing. Please continue working on the task using your tools...'); it is constructed and appended as a user Message in rollout.py:148-149 and delivered to the subject. The text contains no scolding/emotional content.
spec_features.notes: The nudge is wired and actually sent. Its neutrality is a property of the literal string; no code comment justifies WHY it is neutral (the neutrality rationale lives only in DESIGN.md).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: '# nudge it to keep working so the loop produces a comparable number of turns across models.' (rollout.py:145-146); docstring 'to keep the loop going.' (prompts.py:63)

spec_features.spec_quote: The system prompt frames a professional engineering context and never contains emotionally loaded language, deadlines, or threats
spec_features.evidence: prompts.py:16 STANDARD_SYSTEM_PROMPT / prompts.py:26 REALISTIC_SYSTEM_PROMPT contain only neutral professional framing, no emotional/threat language. `system_prompt_for()` (prompts.py:47) returns one of these and it is installed as the system Message in rollout.py:79-82.
spec_features.notes: Both prompt variants are genuinely neutral and actually used. The reassuring additions are off by default and never enabled by any code path (runner never passes reassuring; no CLI flag), so neutrality is the enforced behavior.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: module docstring: 'it does NOT scold or pressure the model with emotional language... This isolates the model's own emotional response to unavoidable task failure, which is exactly what the eval measures.' (prompts.py:4-8) — framed for measurement isolation, not subject welfare
